The proposed 2D-RWTM method is a gridless super-resolution approach for ISAR imaging of moving targets.
The 2D-RWTM method retrieves the sparse scattering points of the target by solving an optimization problem based on atomic norm minimization.
The 2D-RWTM method can handle incomplete ISAR data, where some of the transmitted pulses from different viewing angles are not received.
The 2D-RWTM method forms a 2-Level Toeplitz (2LT) matrix from the received ISAR signal and performs a Vandermonde decomposition to retrieve the 2D frequencies of the scattering points.

The authors investigate the effect of different weighting matrix structures on the performance of the 2D-RWTM method, showing that it can successfully retrieve the scattering point locations with various weighting matrices.

The authors show that the 2D-RWTM method can accurately retrieve the scattering point locations as long as the distance between any two points satisfies a minimum threshold of Δ = 0.45/f1, where f1 is the number of samples in the first dimension.

The authors compare the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of the 2D-RWTM and Atomic Norm Minimization (ANM) methods for ISAR imaging, showing that the 2D-RWTM method achieves lower MSE, indicating better performance.

The key advantage of the 2D-RWTM method is that it is a gridless super-resolution approach, which does not require the scattering points to fit on a predefined grid, leading to lower complexity and higher accuracy.
The use of reweighted trace minimization in the 2D-RWTM method further enhances the sparsity of the retrieved scattering points, leading to improved resolution in the ISAR images.

The Vandermonde decomposition of the 2LT matrix and the Matrix Pencil and Pairing (MaPP) algorithm are the key steps in the 2D-RWTM method that enable the retrieval of 2D frequencies of the scattering points.
The 2D-RWTM method is able to successfully retrieve 18 scattering points with higher Radar Cross Section (RCS) than the others in the ISAR imaging of an Airbus plane.
The authors consider a scenario with 90 noise-free samples randomly selected from a total of 196 complete data samples to evaluate the performance of the 2D-RWTM method.
The 2D-RWTM method is shown to outperform the Atomic Norm Minimization (ANM) method in terms of Mean Squared Error (MSE) for ISAR imaging.

The authors investigate the effect of the proximity of scattering points on the performance of the 2D-RWTM method, showing that it can accurately retrieve the locations as long as the minimum distance between points is satisfied.
The 2D-RWTM method is able to successfully retrieve the 2D frequencies (range and cross-range) of the sparse scattering points in the ISAR imaging of an Airbus plane.
